in grabtown North Carolina the youngest of seven children in a family of poor tobacco sharecroppers her childhood was spent in a modest white farmhouse surrounded by fields of tobacco and cotton in 1925 tragedy struck when the family's barn and cotton Jin burned down forcing them to move to Brogden life grew even harder during the Great Depression as the family moved from place to place her father Jonas took on odd jobs at Sawmills while her mother Molly managed boarding houses for teachers Ava faced a deep personal loss in 1938 when her father died of bronchitis just 15 at the time she Discovery seemed so unreal that mgm's publicity team thought she'd made it up it sounded too much like a script they would invent themselves in August 1941 at just 18 years old Ava boarded a train to Hollywood with her sister bappy as her chaperon she signed a contract with MGM earning $50 a week though it dropped to $35 during layoff periods early on MGM didn't focus on her acting they used her teenagers at the studio MGM tightly controlled her life even requiring permission for her to travel outside Los Angeles soon after arriving in Hollywood Ava met Mickey Rooney on set while he was experiences shaped Ava's resilience in a tough and often unforgiving industry on the other hand Frank Sinatra's Journey with Harry James began in an unexpected and exciting way in June 1939 Sinatra auditioned without any preparation he simply walked up to the piano and started singing his Raw Talent was so remarkable that James immediately signed him for $40 a week just weeks later on June 30th 1939 Sinatra performed his first show with the band at Baltimore's Hippodrome during the seven months he spent with James they recorded 10 songs together including the famous All or Nothing At All Sinatra was eager to join James later admitting I almost broke his arm so he wouldn't get away cuz I was dying to get out of that place but despite their talent the band struggled financially they constantly toured and appeared on non-paying radio shows to stay relevant and James even used up his $7,000 savings borrowed from Benny Goodman to keep the band afloat Sinatra's career took a huge leap forward when he joined Tommy dorsey's band in 1940 this move not only tripled his salary to $125 a week but also marked the start of his rise to fame his first performance with dorsy was on January 26th 1940 at the Coronado theater in Rockford Illinois where he sang Stardust in his first year alone Sinatra recorded over 40 songs with dorsy including his first big hit hulka dots and Moonbeams in April 1940 Sinatra saw dorsy as a father figure but admitted he was intimidated by him saying the only two people I've ever been afraid of are my mother and Tommy dorsy their partnership ended in 1942 but not without drama dorsy demanded 33% of Sinatra's future earnings tensions Rose so high that rumors of mob involvement surfaced though they were never proven Sinatra's personal life also began during these early years he met Nancy barbat in Long Branch New Jersey in the summer of 1934 when he was 19 and she was 17 they married on February 4th 1939 during the Great Depression at the time Nancy worked as a secretary and Sinatra was a singing waiter together they had three children Nancy in 1940 Frank Junior in 1944 and Tina in 1948 Nancy supported Sinatra in every way sewing his bow ties and cooking his favorite meals however as Sinatra's Fame grew so did The Strain on their marriage his infidelities especially his affair with Ava Gardner caused irreparable damage they remained his trusted friend until his death in 1998 in 1943 a young Ava Garder was sitting in a smoky Hollywood club with her husband Mickey Rooney when Frank Sinatra first saw her Sinatra was already a huge star adored by screaming fans and married to Nancy barbato with two children despite both being married there was an instant undeniable spark Gardner was just starting her Hollywood career known more for her beauty than for any acting roles their meeting was brief but it left an impression Sinatra couldn't stop thinking about her and Gardner though trapped in a troubled marriage to Rooney felt the same pull a year later she divorced Rooney citing mental cruelty 6 years later in 1949 they crossed paths again at a glamorous party in Palm Springs hosted by Studio executive Daryl zanak by then Gardner had divorced her second husband Arty Shaw while Sinatra was stuck in an unhappy marriage he spotted her from across the room and greeted her with Jesus you got prettier since last time I saw you their reunion was electric fueled by alcohol which both could handle like pros Garder known for her ability to outdrink almost anyone kept up with Sinatra drink for drink Sinatra had just welcomed a baby with Nancy weeks earlier but that didn't stop him from leaving the party with Garder that night marked the start of their Infamous and fiery Affair one of the wildest episodes in their relationship happened shortly after leaving the party they went on a drunken joy ride to the small town of Indian California in Sinatra's Cadillac somewhere along the way Sinatra pulled out two pistols handing one to Garder in their drunken State they started shooting at street lights and store Windows Gardner even aimed specifically at a hardware store shattering its Windows when the police caught up with them they were shocked to find two of Hollywood's biggest stars holding guns what could have been a career end ing Scandal was quickly smoothed over by a studio publicist who flew in with a mysterious black bag Gardner later claimed that all records of the incident vanished and the officers involved retired early with suspiciously comfortable pensions their Affair became the Talk of the Nation and caused public outrage Sinatra's records were burned by Furious fans and the Roman Catholic Church condemned their relationship His Image as a devoted family man was shattered and his career took a nose dive he lost his contracts with MGM and Colombia records and the public rallied behind his wife Nancy who initially refused to Grant him a divorce Gardner already Infamous for her wild behavior only added to her Legend stories of her Antics like allegedly urinating in the Ritz Lobby fueled her bad girl reputation eventually Nancy gave in and Sinatra and Gardner married in 1951 just a week after his divorce was finalized but it wasn't without interesting stories the day before Ava Gardner and Frank Sinatra's wedding on November 7th 1951 Gardner received an anonymous letter that shook her to her core the letter allegedly from a sex worker claimed to have been in a relationship with Sinatra for months the Revelation left Garder devastated and she later admitted it made her so sick she almost called off the wedding despite her feelings she went through with the ceremony but not without confronting Sinatra Gardner issued a Stern and Unforgettable threat to Sinatra at their wedding reception if you treat me like Nancy I'll kill you their wedding was a small and hurried event in Philadelphia attended by only a few close friends and family in their rush to avoid photographers Gardner forgot her suitcase so during their first honeymoon stop in Miami she had to wear Sinatra's pajamas the Press still managed to Snap photos of them on the beach with gardener dressed in an odd combination of Sinatra's jacket and her travel suit she later called the picture a sad little commentary on our lives in the late 1940s Ava Gardner and Frank Sinatra's careers were headed in completely different directions Gardner was at the top of her game earning $140,000 per movie like in Showboat 1951 Sinatra on the other hand was struggling he had lost his record deal with Colombia records his movie contracts were cancelled and even his agent gave up on him things got so bad that when he bought gifts for Garder he charged them to her own account surprisingly Gardner later said that they were happiest during this tough time she felt that when Sinatra wasn't successful he was Kinder and more grounded but once he found Fame again his old arrogance returned one of the most critical moments in Sinatra's career turnaround was his role in From Here to Eternity Gardner played a big part in helping him get it using a clause in her own Studio contract that required the studio to help her husband she pushed for Sinatra to get a screen test she also cleverly worked through the wife of Columbia Studios Chief Harry con to make it happen the role Sinatra wanted private Angelo magio didn't pay much only $88,000 but it changed everything for him his performance was so good that he won an Oscar and a Golden Globe for best supporting actor in 1954 this marked one of the most remarkable comebacks in Hollywood history their marriage however suffered deeply because of their career struggles and successes during Sinatra's lowest points he fell into severe depression and even attempted suicide several times Garder became the main bread winner which hurt Sinatra's Pride this created tension between them he grew intensely jealous of the men Gardner worked with and sent her daily telegrams while she was filming trying to keep her attention in one dramatic moment in 1968 Sinatra pretended to be Gravely ill to get her to rush to his side after traveling for 24 hours to see him Gardner found out it was just a ploy to be with her in 1950 Ava Gardner went to Spain to film Pandora and the Flying Dutchman while there she he started a fiery affair with bull fighter Mario Cabra cab who barely spoke English dedicated every bull he killed to her when Frank Sinatra arrived in Spain to visit her he brought lavish gifts like six crates of Coca-Cola and an emerald necklace but he discovered her relationship with cab which made him Furious the situation grew so tense that Cabra even threatened to kill Sinatra to avoid violence the film's director secretly sent Cabra away to jerona by 1954 as Gardener's marriage with Sinatra was falling apart she began another intense romance this time with Matador Luis Miguel doingin Gardner described their relationship as a sort of Madness doingin was wealthy and Relentless in his pursuit of her on New Year's Eve in 1953 while Sinatra flew to Madrid to find her she was out partying with doingin and returned home late leaving Sinatra devastated Sinatra's jealousy became uncontrollable he hired private detectives to follow Garder everywhere when she found out it led to explosive fights between them in one incident she hit him with a silver Candlestick knocking him unconscious after discovering he had been spying on her again Sinatra's paranoia also spilled into his behavior with others when he heard that Howard Hughes had spoken to Gardner he drove around Los Angeles with a gun looking for Hughes their home in Pacific Palisades turned into a constant Battlefield with fights that included screaming throwing objects and public outbursts at one point Sinatra barged into a Beverly Hills restaurant where Gardner was dining with Lana Turner and shouting lesbians you're all godamn lesbians their fights shocked everyone around them and sometimes escalated to embarrassing levels in one shocking moment Sinatra threw a water-filled douche at Gardner and Lana Turner their fights happened everywhere at home in taxis in restaurants and even during social events during a play at London's Cambridge theater Sinatra attacked a photographer rolling on the floor with him before dragging him outside their fights also disrupted others lives once during a car ride with Richard atenor and his wife Sheila Sim Sinatra and Gardner erupted into a heated argument about his habit of signing autographs Gardner later admitted I'm possessive and jealous and so is Frank he has a temper that bursts into flames while mine Burns inside for hours their neighbors often heard the chaos from their home with shouting broken objects and slammed doors becoming a regular occurrence their relationship was a whirlwind of passion and even when things reached their Breaking Point Ava Gardner and Frank Sinatra shared a bond that endured though they divorced in 1957 their connection remained strong and full of unique gestures every year on her birthday Sinatra would send Garder Grand bouquets of flowers a tradition he kept up until her death they occasionally reunited like in 1959 when Gardner was in Australia filming on the beach Sinatra flew across the world officially for concerts in Melbourne and Sydney but it was clear his real reason was to see her they managed to steal a couple of private night together despite being hounded by the Press though their brief reunion didn't leave enough time for old arguments to resurface as Gardner Riley noted in her autobiography Sinatra's respect for Gardner was evident even as he moved on with his life before marrying Mia faroh in 1966 Sinatra insured Gardner was informed first showing her the same courtesy when he married Barbara Marx in 1976 Gardner responded to news of his marriage to Pharaoh with her sharp wit joking that she always expected Sinatra to end up in bed with a little boy despite their separation Sinatra kept Gardener close in his thoughts her photo remained taped to his dressing room mirror and in his homes he dedicated small shrines to her complete with statues photos and even a painting with a candle that he lit daily when Gardner's Health declined in her later years Sinatra's support was constant after two strokes in 1986 left her struggling he stepped in to make sure she received the best care though she was financially secure Sinatra insisted on paying her medical bills which totaled $250,000 a year he also arranged for a private medically equipped jet to bring her from London to Los Angeles to see Specialists even when Gardner could no longer speak easily Sinatra would call her talking enough for both of them while nurses held the phone to her ear he'd remind her how much he loved her and share his own struggles with aging on her bedside table Gardner kept a cherished photo of their younger days together she passed away from pneumonia on January 25th 1990 at age 67 their love left a lasting mark on both of them Garder once gave Sinatra a watch inscribed with the words to Frank and desert Knights Ava a reference to their time together in Palm Springs even after remarrying Sinatra never truly let go of her memory when Gardner passed he was heartbroken and chose to grieve in private covering all her funeral expenses but skipping the ceremony their relationship full of fiery highs and painful lows became a Hollywood Legend Sinatra once admitted anything that burned that hot was bound to burn out but while it was going on I was having a ball Gardner in turn called Sinatra the love of my life and believed they were lovers forever eternally despite their divorce their connection evolved into a deep enduring love that lasted until the very end
